item.title: #3583021: Remove the ai_tools_property_alter hook implementation superseded by the schema property converter
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583021 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

The tool_ai_connector module's hook_ai_tools_property_alter() implementation has been removed, along with its service registration. This hook used to expand one level of map properties onto a tool's advertised schema, but it only ever fired on a code path that the tool module's bridge no longer uses: the bridge builds its schema properties directly from the tool's JSON Schema output, which already covers nested maps, list inputs, and constraint-derived keywords that the old hook never handled. For sites and modules using the supported bridge (ToolPluginBase::normalize()), nothing changes; schemas are generated the same way they already were.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Removed Drupal\tool_ai_connector\Hook\AiToolsPropertyHooks (the hook_ai_tools_property_alter() implementation) and its service registration; no replacement is needed on the supported bridge path.

Technical details

The hook (AiToolsPropertyHooks::aiToolsPropertyAlter()), its #[Hook('ai_tools_property_alter')] attribute, the legacy procedural bridge function in tool_ai_connector.module, and the service registration in tool_ai_connector.services.yml were all deleted. The hook only fired when a MapDataDefinition-backed property was normalized via the ai module's default FunctionCallBase::normalize(), which routes through Utility\ContextDefinitionNormalizer. The tool bridge's own ToolPluginBase::normalize() overrides that method and instead builds properties from the tool's emitted JSON Schema via SchemaToolsPropertyConverter, so for every tool-bridged function call, the hook's instanceof MapContextDefinition branch was dead code. Removing it also clears a straggler reference to MapContextDefinition, a class slated for deprecation and removal in the context-system detach plan tracked in #3583016.

Coverage for the removal landed as a new kernel test, MapListAdvertisementTest, which asserts the bridge advertises complete schemas without the hook: a map input with nested maps produces object schemas with properties at every depth, a multiple-value input advertises an array with an items schema, and a free-form map (no declared properties) advertises a plain object rather than an empty or untyped schema.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">A third-party function-call plugin that routed tool definition objects through ai.context_definition_normalizer directly (rather than through the tool bridge's normalize()) loses the one-level map expansion the removed hook provided. Switch to the supported path, the bridge's ToolPluginBase::normalize(), which builds properties from the tool's JSON Schema via SchemaToolsPropertyConverter and covers nested maps, lists, and constraint-derived keywords that the old hook did not.

item.title: #3583041: Issue #3583041: Keep a multiple definition's description on the array
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583041 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

The Tool module builds JSON Schema descriptions of each tool's inputs, which are consumed by AI agents and MCP clients to know what a tool accepts. For inputs that accept multiple values (multiple: TRUE), the schema generator previously threw away the field's own description and title, replacing them with a generic Array of <label> string, while duplicating the real label and description onto the nested items schema instead. This meant the actual, useful description written by the tool's author was hidden one level down instead of appearing where a caller would look for it. The fix keeps the field's real title and description on the array schema itself, where they belong, and leaves items to describe only the type of each element.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: For context definitions with multiple: TRUE, ContextDefinitionNormalizer no longer duplicates the label/description onto items or rewrites the array's own description as Array of <label>; the definition's real description and title now stay directly on the array schema, and items carries only its type (and constraints like format).

Technical details

The bug was in ContextDefinitionNormalizer::normalize() in the tool module: when handling a multiple context definition, the code cloned the item definition, normalized it to build items, then copied that clone's description onto items['description'] and synthesized $schema['description'] = 'Array of ' . $object->getLabel(), overwriting whatever description the array schema already had.

The fix clears the label and description on the cloned single-item definition before normalizing it ($item_definition->setLabel(''); $item_definition->setDescription('');), so items no longer picks up a redundant title/description, and removes the block that rewrote $schema['description'] to the generic Array of ... string. The array's own title and description, already set earlier in the method from the definition, are left untouched. Kernel tests in InputSchemaMatrixTest and RicherSchemaEmissionTest were updated to assert the corrected shape, e.g. a multi_string field now emits {"items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "Multi string: A multiple string input.", "title": "Multi string"} instead of nesting the description inside items and replacing the top-level description with "Array of Multi string".</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Code or tests that assert on the exact JSON Schema produced for multiple tool inputs must be updated. For example, a multi_string field's schema changes from:

{
  "type": ["array", "null"],
  "items": {
    "type": "string",
    "description": "Multi string: A multiple string input.",
    "title": "Multi string"
  },
  "description": "Array of Multi string",
  "title": "Multi string"
}

to:

{
  "type": ["array", "null"],
  "items": { "type": "string" },
  "description": "Multi string: A multiple string input.",
  "title": "Multi string"
}

Contribution

item.title: #3583029: Enforce required outputs in ToolBase::execute() so a success cannot omit a declared output
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583029 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

The Tool API's OutputDefinition has always defaulted required to TRUE, but nothing enforced it: a tool could return ExecutableResult::success() without setting one of its own required outputs and execute() would report success anyway. A caller would only discover the problem later, either from an exception when reading the missing value or, worse, not at all if it just read the raw context values off the formatted result. Now execute() validates the outputs right after a successful doExecute() and, if a required output is missing or a set value doesn't match its declared shape, replaces the result with a failure categorized as Runtime and logs the violation against the tool. This closes the gap that had forced the MCP Server Tool Bridge module to omit required from the JSON Schema it advertises for tool outputs, since it could not promise something the Tool API itself did not guarantee.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ToolBase::execute() now fails a tool (with FailureCategory::Runtime) instead of silently succeeding when a doExecute() implementation omits a declared required output, sets it to NULL, or sets a value that violates its output definition.

Technical details

The check lives in a new private ToolBase::failOnOutputViolations(), called from execute() immediately after the loop that copies matching context values into $this->outputs. It calls the existing validateOutputs() and, if the returned ConstraintViolationList is non-empty, logs the violation against the tool's plugin ID and overwrites $this->result with ExecutableResult::failure(..., FailureCategory::Runtime), since a missing or malformed output is a bug in the tool, not something the caller can fix by changing its arguments.

TypedOutputsTrait::validateOutputs() was rewritten to check shape as well as presence: an output whose Context::hasContextValue() is false now counts as unset (previously only a wholly-absent key did, so a required output explicitly set to NULL slipped through), and each set value is run through a new private validateOutputValue() that mirrors TypedInputsTrait::validateInputValue(). Multiple-value and ListOutputDefinition outputs are checked item by item with the failing index named in the message; MapOutputDefinition properties are checked individually, with missing required properties reported by name; and entity-typed outputs (data type entity or entity:*) are only checked for being an EntityInterface instance, not run through full entity field validation, so a tool that merely returns an entity it loaded is not failed for that entity's own data problems. The item/property-naming helper and the core TypedDataManager prototype-cache workaround (for the upstream bug in drupal/drupal#3616328) were extracted from TypedInputsTrait into a new shared ValueViolationsTrait, used by both input and output validation.

Test coverage was added via two new fixture plugins, RequiredOutputTool and EntityOutputTool, plus tests/src/Kernel/Tool/OutputValidationTest.php and additions to ToolBaseTest, covering a missing or NULL required output failing with the output named, an omitted optional output still succeeding, an invalid output value failing the same way, and entity outputs being validated by shape rather than by full field validation.

Upgrade

Any tool plugin whose doExecute() can return a success without setting a value for one of its declared output_definitions will now fail instead. For each such output, either always set it:

protected function doExecute(array $values): ExecutableResult {
  // Make sure every required output is set on every success path.
  return ExecutableResult::success($message, ['answer' => $computed_value]);
}

or mark it optional in the plugin's output_definitions if it legitimately may not always have a value:

output_definitions: [
  'link' => new OutputDefinition(
    data_type: 'uri',
    label: new TranslatableMarkup('Link'),
    description: new TranslatableMarkup('An optional uri output.'),
    required: FALSE,
  ),
],

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 19, 2026

  • dcgoodwin (CivicActions)
  • mglaman (Acquia)
  • michaellander

item.title: #3583033: Add ToolDefinitionSerializer::normalizeOutputSchema() as the twin of normalizeInputSchema()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583033 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

The Tool API module's ToolDefinitionSerializer already had normalizeInputSchema() to build a full JSON Schema object for a tool's inputs, but no equivalent for outputs, just a bare properties list. Consumers that needed a full output schema, such as the MCP server tool bridge and a hand-built OpenAPI generator, ended up reimplementing the wrapper themselves and getting details wrong, like omitting required outputs or mishandling the empty-properties case. This issue adds normalizeOutputSchema() as the output-side twin, so any module building on Tool API can get a correct, consistent output schema without re-solving the same problems.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New ToolDefinitionSerializer::normalizeOutputSchema() method returns a complete JSON Schema object (type, properties, required) for a tool's declared outputs.

Technical details

normalizeOutputSchema(ToolInterface $tool, string $format = 'json_schema'): array wraps normalizeOutputDefinitions() in {type: object, properties: ...} and adds a required array populated from each OutputDefinition::isRequired(), guarding the empty case with new \ArrayObject() so it serializes to {} rather than [], mirroring normalizeInputSchema().

The one deliberate asymmetry: normalizeInputSchema() sets additionalProperties: FALSE because a tool rejects unknown arguments, but normalizeOutputSchema() leaves it unset. The docblock explains why: ToolBase::execute() only copies declared outputs into the outputs bag, but getFormattedResult() deliberately passes undeclared result values through, so a serialized result can legitimately carry members beyond the declared properties, and closing the schema would make it lie. A kernel test (OutputSchemaTest) covers both the normal case, asserting required only lists outputs marked required, and the no-output case, asserting the empty properties bag encodes as {}.

The required list is currently advisory: nothing in ToolBase::execute() yet enforces that a tool actually returns its required outputs. That enforcement landed separately as commit 1ab3f3e for the follow-up issue referenced in this one (#3583029).

Contribution

item.title: #3582991: Drush tool:run should surface access denial reason and pre-flight validation
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3582991 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

The tool:run Drush command now tells you why it refused to run a tool instead of a generic "Access denied" message. It validates the tool's inputs first, so a bad or missing argument is reported as an input problem rather than a permission problem, and when access truly is denied, it surfaces the actual reason the tool gave (for example, which permission is missing). With --json, every pre-execution failure now also includes a machine-readable error_type field, useful for scripts, CI pipelines, or AI agents driving Drush programmatically.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The tool:run Drush command's --json error output gains a new error_type field (backed by the RunErrorType enum), and now validates tool inputs before checking access rather than after.

Technical details

ToolRunCommand::run() in the tool module now calls $tool->validateInputs() before checking access, since access() fails closed with a generic reason on invalid input; checking access first would misreport a bad argument as a permission problem. If violations exist, the command reports them and exits before ever calling access().

The access check itself now calls $tool->access(return_as_object: TRUE) and, when the result implements AccessResultReasonInterface, appends getReason() to the error message instead of dropping it.

Every failure path in the command now passes a new RunErrorType backed enum (src/Drush/RunErrorType.php) to writeError(), which serializes it as error_type in the --json output: tool_not_found, invalid_option, user_not_found, user_blocked, invalid_input, access_denied, and execution_failed. A tool that runs and reports its own failure (a failed ExecutableResult) is not one of these: it has no error_type, since that's a result, not a command error. The docs at docs/usage/drush.md document the ordering, the JSON shape, and each error type. A new test fixture, InvalidOutputTool, exercises the one execution failure ToolBase doesn't absorb: a result whose output value doesn't fit its output definition, which makes execute() itself throw after doExecute() already succeeded.

Upgrade

Scripts or CI pipelines invoking drush tool:run --json and inspecting failures should switch from string-matching the error message to reading the new error_type field:

{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Access denied for tool 'send_email': The 'send emails' permission is required.",
  "error_type": "access_denied"
}

Possible error_type values: tool_not_found, invalid_option, user_not_found, user_blocked, invalid_input, access_denied, execution_failed. Note that a tool which runs and reports its own failure has no error_type at all, that document is a result (success: false plus the tool's own message), not a command error.

Contribution

  • Opened: August 11, 2026

item.title: #3583038: Allow output definitions to declare examples
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583038 · 1 contributor · 7 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

Tool API input definitions could already carry illustrative "examples" values (e.g. a status field's example values draft, completed), but output definitions could not. This mattered for anyone generating an OpenAPI document or an MCP outputSchema from Tool API definitions: every request property could carry an example, but no response property could. This issue extends the same examples capability to outputs, so a tool's output schema can now show a client what a value looks like after it is published.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Any class implementing OutputDefinitionInterface directly (without extending one of the module's four output classes) must now also implement getExamples() and setExamples(), e.g. by using the new ExamplesTrait.
  • New API: OutputDefinitionInterface gains getExamples()/setExamples(), and OutputDefinition/EntityOutputDefinition gain an examples constructor argument, so tool outputs (not just inputs) can declare illustrative example values, emitted as the examples keyword in generated JSON Schema/OpenAPI output.

Technical details

The examples property and its accessors, previously hard-coded into InputDefinitionTrait, were extracted into a new standalone ExamplesTrait. InputDefinitionTrait now composes ExamplesTrait so input behavior is unchanged, and OutputDefinitionInterface declares getExamples()/setExamples(), implemented via the same ExamplesTrait in all four output classes (OutputDefinition, EntityOutputDefinition, MapOutputDefinition, ListOutputDefinition). OutputDefinition and EntityOutputDefinition (the scalar/entity leaf classes) also gained an examples constructor argument, mirroring InputDefinition and EntityInputDefinition, so a #[Tool] attribute can declare output examples inline; the map and list output classes don't take the argument directly since their examples live on their child definitions.

ContextDefinitionNormalizer::getSchemaProperty() (or its equivalent private schema-building method) now checks for OutputDefinitionInterface alongside InputDefinitionInterface when deciding whether to emit the examples keyword: if (!$object->isMultiple() && ($object instanceof InputDefinitionInterface || $object instanceof OutputDefinitionInterface) && ($examples = $object->getExamples())) { $schema['examples'] = array_values($examples); }. Examples are read off the post-transform definition, so an output example shows the value as it is actually published to a client, and a definition swapped out by a ToolOutputDefinitionNormalizeEvent subscriber loses its examples unless the subscriber re-sets them. As with inputs, a multiple output's examples land on the items sub-schema rather than the array level.

A follow-up, referenced in the issue body, is tracked to let #[ToolProperty] and #[ToolOutput] attributes take an example argument the way #[ToolInput] already does.

Upgrade

Any class that implements OutputDefinitionInterface directly, rather than extending OutputDefinition, EntityOutputDefinition, MapOutputDefinition, or ListOutputDefinition, must add getExamples()/setExamples(), most simply by adding use ExamplesTrait;:

use Drupal\tool\TypedData\ExamplesTrait;

class MyOutputDefinition implements OutputDefinitionInterface {
  use ExamplesTrait;
  // ...
}

To declare example values on an output:

$output = new OutputDefinition(
  data_type: 'string',
  label: new TranslatableMarkup('Status'),
  description: new TranslatableMarkup('The order status.'),
  examples: ['draft', 'completed'],
);

Contribution

item.title: #3583017: Re-parent the definition families onto typed data behind a temporary ContextDefinitionInterface bridge
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583017 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

The tool module's input and output definition classes (InputDefinition, OutputDefinition, and their Map/List/Entity variants) now inherit from Drupal core's typed data system (DataDefinition, MapDataDefinition, ListDataDefinition, EntityDataDefinition) instead of from the Plugin Context system. This is an internal architectural step towards fully detaching tool definitions from Drupal's context API; it does not change constructor signatures, JSON Schema output, or any other observable behavior. MapContextDefinition and ListContextDefinition are now deprecated in favor of the corresponding MapInputDefinition/MapOutputDefinition and ListInputDefinition/ListOutputDefinition classes, and will be removed in a future release.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Tool's input/output definition classes (InputDefinition, OutputDefinition, and Map/List/Entity variants) now extend Drupal core typed data classes instead of Plugin Context classes; instanceof ContextDefinition/EntityContextDefinition checks against them no longer match.
  • Deprecation: Drupal\tool\TypedData\MapContextDefinition and ListContextDefinition are deprecated in tool:1.0.0-beta10 and removed in tool:1.0.0-rc1; use MapInputDefinition/MapOutputDefinition and ListInputDefinition/ListOutputDefinition instead.

Technical details

This is step 1 of a 3-step plan (parent plan #3583016) to detach the tool module's definition classes from core's Plugin Context system. Each definition class now extends the matching typed data class rather than a context class, for example InputDefinition extends DataDefinition and EntityInputDefinition/EntityDefinitionBase extends EntityDataDefinition. To avoid breaking the three remaining context-coupled internals (Context storage in the input/output traits, ContextDefinitionNormalizer matching, and the ai module boundary), every class still implements ContextDefinitionInterface, with the missing methods supplied by a new ContextDefinitionBridgeTrait: isMultiple()/setMultiple(), getDefaultValue()/setDefaultValue(), a compatible setRequired(), getDataDefinition() (rebuilds a core definition via the typed data manager, needed because Context::getContextData() validates against its constraints), and a stub isSatisfiedBy() that builds a core ContextDefinition on demand since nothing in the tool stack calls it directly.

A key subtlety is getConstraints(): DataDefinition::getConstraints() would merge in TypedDataManager::getDefaultConstraints() (PrimitiveType, NotNull for required fields, data type constraints, AllowedValues), but ContextDefinitionNormalizer iterates getConstraints() to build the published JSON Schema, so the bridge trait overrides it to return only author-declared constraints, preserving the old ContextDefinition-style behavior. The base classes MapDefinitionBase and ListDefinitionBase now carry the property/item-definition handling that used to come from MapContextDefinition/ListContextDefinition by inheritance, and those two classes are thinned to deprecated subclasses that trigger E_USER_DEPRECATED on construction.

Because instanceof ContextDefinition and instanceof EntityContextDefinition no longer match these classes, this is flagged as an API change, though the issue notes no known usages outside the tool module itself. The bridge trait and the ContextDefinitionInterface parentage are marked @internal and will be removed in #3583019 once #3583018 detaches Context storage and the normalizer.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Replace deprecated classes with their typed-data-based replacements:

// Before
new \Drupal\tool\TypedData\MapContextDefinition(...)
new \Drupal\tool\TypedData\ListContextDefinition(...)

// After
new \Drupal\tool\TypedData\MapInputDefinition(...)   // or MapOutputDefinition
new \Drupal\tool\TypedData\ListInputDefinition(...)  // or ListOutputDefinition

Code that does instanceof \Drupal\Core\Plugin\Context\ContextDefinition or instanceof \Drupal\Core\Plugin\Context\EntityContextDefinition against tool's input/output definitions will no longer match; check against \Drupal\tool\TypedData\InputDefinitionInterface or OutputDefinitionInterface instead.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 12, 2026

item.title: #3562612: Add the possibility to add logo/image for a tool
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3562612 · 3 contributors · 13 comments
  • Followers: 3
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

Tool plugins can now declare an icon, making it easier to build tool pickers, automation UIs, and agent surfaces that need a visual to scan through long lists of tools. Rather than inventing a tool-specific image system, the module hooks into Drupal core's Icon API (available in Drupal 11.1+), so any icon pack a module or theme already declares can be reused. The Tool Explorer module's listing page now shows each tool's icon, falling back to a generic icon based on the tool's operation type (read, transform, destructive, etc.) when a tool declares none.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: #[Tool] attribute and ToolDefinition gain an optional icon argument/getIcon(): ?string method for referencing a core Icon API icon (pack_id:icon_id).

Technical details

The #[Tool] attribute gains an optional icon argument: a string in the form pack_id:icon_id referencing an icon declared in any module or theme's *.icons.yml file. Because it's a plain string, it's a valid constant expression for use in attributes, and because it's stored as a regular definition property, a deriver can set a different icon per derivative, which was the original motivation for supporting MCP/derived tools with distinct icons.

ToolDefinition::getIcon(): ?string simply returns the stored reference verbatim. Nothing is resolved or validated at plugin discovery time; the module still supports core ^10.5, and the Icon API only exists from 11.1 onward, so validating early would break on older cores. Resolution is left entirely to consumers, who go through Drupal\Core\Theme\Icon\IconDefinition (or plugin.manager.icon_pack) and are expected to treat a missing pack, missing icon, or pre-11.1 core the same way: as "no icon".

ToolExplorerController::buildIcon() demonstrates this pattern: it feature-detects IconDefinition::class before doing anything, and for a tool that declares no icon it falls back to tool:operation-<operation value>, a small icon pack shipped in tool.icons.yml with one SVG per ToolOperation case. This fallback is presentation-only and never touches the definition itself, so other consumers such as the MCP bridge still see NULL and can apply their own defaults.

Upgrade

To declare an icon for a tool plugin, add the icon argument to the #[Tool] attribute, referencing an icon pack declared in a *.icons.yml file:

#[Tool(
  id: 'my_tool',
  label: new TranslatableMarkup('My Tool'),
  description: new TranslatableMarkup('Does something.'),
  operation: ToolOperation::Transform,
  icon: 'my_module:my_icon',
)]

This is additive; existing tool plugins without an icon argument continue to work, and ToolDefinition::getIcon() returns NULL for them.

item.title: #3585919: Nested empty object schemas still serialize as [] because normalizeObjectSchema() only normalizes the top level
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585919 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

The MCP Server module builds JSON Schema definitions for each registered tool and sends them to connecting MCP clients. An empty properties map is indistinguishable from an empty array in PHP, and a prior fix (#3585899) made sure the top-level properties of a tool's input schema always serializes as a JSON object ({}) rather than an array ([]). This issue found that the fix only checked the top level: a nested empty object, for example a free-form opts parameter, still serialized as [] several levels down. Strict MCP clients reject schemas with an array where an object is required, so a tool declaring such a nested parameter could fail to register with those clients. The fix makes the normalization recursive so every nested schema position, not just the top level, is corrected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

McpServerFactory::normalizeObjectSchema() previously converted only the schema's top-level properties value. It now delegates to a new normalizeSchema() helper that walks every JSON Schema keyword that can hold a sub-schema: single sub-schema keywords (additionalProperties, contains, if/then/else, not, propertyNames, contentSchema, etc.), map keywords (properties, $defs, definitions, patternProperties, dependentSchemas), and list keywords (allOf, anyOf, oneOf, prefixItems), recursing into each. items and draft-07 dependencies get special-cased handling since each can hold either a single sub-schema or a list, and an empty array means something different in each case (items: [] is the empty schema, allOf: [] is a valid empty list). Any sub-schema that is an empty PHP array is replaced with \stdClass so it serializes as {}.

The module's tests/modules/mcp_server_test gained a NestedSchemaTool fixture that declares empty object schemas in every nested position (items, additionalProperties, anyOf, $ref targets in $defs, contentSchema, dependencies), and ToolSchemaNormalizationTest asserts each one decodes back as \stdClass rather than an empty list.

Two things called out in the issue were left out of scope deliberately: registerTools() still passes a tool's outputSchema through without normalization, so a top-level empty outputSchema.properties still serializes as [] (tracked separately per the issue); and normalizeObjectSchema() still unconditionally overwrites $schema['type'] to 'object', silently masking a tool that declared a different type instead of surfacing the SDK's InvalidArgumentException.

item.title: #3585870: Tool definition from the plugin deriver all have the same label ("Tool API")
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585870 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

In the MCP Server module, a Tool plugin can use a deriver to expose several dynamic tools from one class, for example the Tool API bridge exposing each configured Tool API tool as its own MCP tool. Previously every one of those derived tools showed the same label, "Tool API", because the deriver had no way to give each derivative its own name; it just inherited the base plugin's label. Now a deriver must supply a distinct label for each derivative, so clients see the actual name of each tool instead of a single repeated generic label.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ToolDefinition::withDerivative() now requires a label argument for each derivative, and description must be a TranslatableMarkup (no longer accepts a raw string).

Technical details

The bug was in ToolDefinition::withDerivative(): the clone it built always reused $this->label from the base definition, with no parameter to override it, while other fields like description and inputSchema could already be overridden per derivative. The fix adds a required TranslatableMarkup $label parameter, since (per the updated docblock) "the base label names the family of tools, never one derivative, so each derivative names itself," matching how core's block and local task derivers behave.

While changing the signature, the method was also generalized: outputSchema, readOnly, and idempotent are now overridable per derivative too (previously only description, inputSchema, and destructive were), and every optional parameter uniformly uses "NULL keeps the base value" instead of withDerivative() special-casing description's type. The description parameter's type also narrowed from TranslatableMarkup|string|null to ?TranslatableMarkup; a deriver that builds a description from config text is now expected to wrap it itself with new TranslatableMarkup('@text', ['@text' => $text]) so config values are never accidentally used as translation source strings. Coverage for the new withDerivative() contract lives in ToolDefinitionTest.

item.title: #3583025: Show requirement status in tool:info, tool:list, and tool:search
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583025 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

The Tool module's Drush commands now show whether each tool is actually ready to run. drush tool:list and drush tool:search gain a Requirements column showing Met or the reason it is not (for example, a missing API key), plus a new --unmet option (show, the default; hide; or only) to filter the listing. drush tool:info gains a Requirements: line in its table and markdown output, and a requirements key ({"met": ..., "message": ...}) in its JSON output. Previously a builder had no way to see a tool would fail until they actually ran it with tool:run; now the listing and info commands surface that up front. None of the commands change their exit code based on requirement status: tool:list and tool:search still exit 0 for an empty or fully-filtered result, and tool:info still exits 0 for a tool whose requirements are unmet, since these commands answer "what exists" and "what is this", not "can it run".

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: tool:list, tool:search, and tool:info Drush commands report each tool's checkRequirements() status; tool:list/tool:search gain a --unmet=show|hide|only filter option and tool:info --format=json gains a requirements key.

Technical details

The three commands share one probe: the new @internal Drupal\tool\Drush\RequirementStatus value object. Its static forTool() instantiates the plugin via ToolManager::createInstance() (passing a DrushInvoker) and calls checkRequirements(). A caught RequirementsException produces an unmet status carrying the exception message; any other \Throwable (for example a broken create()) is also caught and reported as unmet with a Could not instantiate tool: ... message, so one plugin with a broken service dependency cannot take down the entire listing. label() renders Met or the message for table/markdown output, and toArray() produces the JSON shape.

ToolOutputTrait gained requirementStatuses() (probes every listed definition) and filterByRequirementStatus(), driven by the new @internal UnmetFilter enum (Show, Hide, Only), whose keeps() method encodes the filtering logic and whose tryFrom() validates the raw --unmet option value, exiting 1 with the same message shape as an invalid --operation on failure. ToolInfoCommand::buildSchemas() now returns NULL instead of throwing when createInstance() fails, so tool:info on a tool whose create() throws still reports its status and omits input_schema/output_schema rather than erroring out.

The test module tool_test gained broken_constructor_tool, a plugin whose create() unconditionally throws, used to exercise the instantiation-failure path in the new RequirementStatusTest and in the command kernel tests. This work builds on the DrushInvoker machinery introduced in #3583023.

No upgrade steps are needed for module users; this only adds output and an option to existing Drush commands. Scripts parsing tool:info --format=json can now read the new requirements key:

"requirements": {"met": false, "message": "Test API key is not configured."}

item.title: #3585912: STDIO tool calls execute without an authenticated user, so permission-gated tools fail
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585912 · 1 contributor · 22 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

Previously, drush mcp:server (the STDIO transport used by AI clients like Claude Desktop) ran every tool call as the anonymous user, so any permission-gated tool (most entity or configuration reads/writes) silently failed access checks. The command now requires a Drupal account argument, a user name or numeric ID, and runs the whole session as that account, so permission checks evaluate correctly. Passing 0 still allows an explicit anonymous session. Existing MCP client configurations and manual invocations that call mcp:server with no argument will now fail with an error rather than silently running as anonymous, so they need to be updated to pass an account. Running the command from an interactive terminal without an argument now opens a user picker instead of failing.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: Minimum Drush version for the STDIO transport raised from 12.x to 13.
  • API change: drush mcp:server now takes a required account argument (user name or numeric ID, or 0 for anonymous); invocations that omit it now error instead of running as anonymous.

Technical details

The fix is in McpServerCommands::server(), which gained a required account positional argument. loadAccount() resolves it: '0' becomes an AnonymousUserSession, an all-digit value loads the user by ID, anything else is looked up by user name via entity_type.manager's user storage; blocked or unresolvable accounts throw before the transport is created. The resolved account is applied with the account_switcher service (AccountSwitcherInterface::switchTo()), and switchBack() runs in a finally block so the process-global account is always restored.

A Drush #[CLI\Hook(type: HookManager::INTERACT, ...)] hook, interactAccount(), handles the case where the argument is omitted: if STDIN is a TTY (a real terminal, not an MCP client's pipes), it prompts with $this->io()->search() against matchUsers() (a fuzzy, access-check-free lookup over active user names); otherwise Symfony's normal missing-argument error is reported on STDERR before the server is built, so nothing corrupts the STDIO transport. The README.md and the mcp_server_test module's new test_current_user tool (which reports the acting uid, name, and a permission check) were added to support this. The change also bumps the documented minimum Drush version for STDIO to 13.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Update any MCP client configuration or manual invocation of the STDIO transport to pass an account:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "drupal": {
      "command": "vendor/bin/drush",
      "args": ["mcp:server", "admin"]
    }
  }
}

or from the shell:

drush mcp:server admin

Use drush mcp:server 0 to keep running as anonymous. Also confirm the site runs Drush 13 or higher for the STDIO transport.

Summary

The Tool module's drush tool:info <id> --format=json command previously reduced every input and output to a bare data type (string, map, etc.), with no way to see that a field only accepts a fixed set of values, or what keys a map input expects. Now the JSON output also includes input_schema and output_schema keys with the full JSON Schema for the tool, so a script or AI agent reading this command's output can discover enum choices, numeric ranges, formats, and nested map properties before invoking the tool. item.title: #3585923: Session lock is released before streamed (SSE) responses finish
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585923 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

MCP Server's per-session lock, introduced to stop two requests from touching the same session at once, was being released too early for streamed (SSE) responses. Because the SDK does its actual work later, while the response is being sent, a second request could sneak in and read or write session state while the first request was still streaming. On PostgreSQL sites using the database lock backend this also produced a nastier symptom: a tool that opened a database transaction and then suspended could have its later rollback resurrect the just-deleted lock row, forcing the next request on that session to wait out the entire lock lease and hit client-side timeouts. This is fixed so the lock is now held for the full duration of the streamed response.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Session lock could be released while an SSE (streamed) response was still running, letting a concurrent request read or write the same MCP session's state.

Technical details

The fix is in McpServerController::handle(). Previously the lock release lived only in the method's finally block, which runs as soon as the controller returns, before a StreamedResponse's callback has actually executed. Now, when the transport's PSR response body is not seekable (the SSE path), the controller wraps the StreamedResponse's existing callback in a new closure that calls the original callback and releases $lock_name in its own finally, so the lock lives until the SDK's Fiber-driven stream actually completes or throws. A new $release_lock flag tells the controller's outer finally to skip releasing the lock itself in that case, since the wrapped callback now owns that responsibility. Non-streamed responses and exceptions thrown before a response is produced still release the lock the old way. If a streamed response is constructed but never sent, its callback never runs and thus never releases the lock explicitly. That case relies on LockBackendInterface::releaseAll(), which DatabaseLockBackend registers as a shutdown function, as covered by the new testUnsentStreamedResponseLockIsFreedByReleaseAll kernel test. A companion test, testStreamedResponseHoldsSessionLockUntilSent, drives a tool that suspends inside a Fiber and a real DatabaseLockBackend, asserting the lock is still held after the controller returns and only released once $response->sendContent() finishes.

  • Status: Fixed

The mcp_server module removed McpToolSamplingTrait, a convenience helper that tool plugins could use to ask the AI client to generate text (LLM "sampling"). The trait, its test coverage, and the test-only SamplingEchoTool fixture are gone. This was done because the underlying mcp/sdk package (0.8+) marked its own Sampling feature as deprecated, and the module, still in beta, does not carry deprecated code forward with a transition period. Sites and custom tools that used this trait need to update their code; everything else about the module is unaffected.

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Drupal\mcp_server\Traits\McpToolSamplingTrait and its sample() helper were removed; tools that requested LLM sampling must call ClientGateway::sample() directly.
  • Deprecation: No deprecation period was provided before removal, per the module's beta no-BC-layers policy.

The fix deletes src/Traits/McpToolSamplingTrait.php, its kernel test tests/src/Kernel/Traits/McpToolSamplingTraitTest.php, and the fixture tests/modules/mcp_server_test/src/Plugin/mcp_server/Tool/SamplingEchoTool.php that exercised it. final class MyTool extends ToolPluginBase implements ClientGatewayAwareInterface {
  use McpToolSamplingTrait;

  public function execute(array $arguments, ClientGateway $gateway): mixed {
    $this->setClientGateway($gateway);
    $result = $this->sample($arguments['prompt'] ?? '', 500);
    // ...
  }
}

  public function execute(array $arguments, ClientGateway $gateway): mixed {
    $result = $gateway->sample($arguments['prompt'] ?? '', 500);
    // ...
  }

item.title: #3436728: Check the status of a consumer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 6.1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +176/−7 · php +175/−6 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 14da180
  • Discussion: #3436728 · 7 contributors · 25 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Simple OAuth now checks whether an OAuth client (a "consumer" entity) is published before granting it access. Previously, unpublishing a consumer did not actually stop it from working: it could still request new access tokens via the client credentials or refresh token grants, and tokens it had already obtained kept working against protected resources. Now an unpublished consumer is treated as if it doesn't exist: attempts to obtain a token fail with an invalid_client error, and requests bearing a token issued by a now-disabled client are rejected with "The client is disabled." The client selection dropdown in the client credentials token creation form also stops listing unpublished consumers.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Unpublished (disabled) consumers can no longer obtain new OAuth tokens or use previously issued bearer tokens; this closes an access control gap.
  • Requirements: Minimum drupal/consumers dependency raised to ^1.24 for the consumer entity status field.

Technical details

The fix relies on the status field added to the consumer entity by the consumers module (see #3436723), and bumps the drupal/consumers dependency to ^1.24 to guarantee its availability.

ClientRepository::getClientEntity() now adds 'status' => 1 to the loadByProperties() lookup used to find a consumer by client_id, so an unpublished consumer resolves to no client entity at all, which makes validateClient() return FALSE for both the client credentials and refresh token grant types. Oauth2ClientCredentialsTokenCreateForm applies the same status condition to the client entity query and the storage lookup used during validation, so unpublished consumers disappear from the form's client list.

For tokens issued before a consumer was unpublished, SimpleOauthAuthenticationProvider::authenticate() now calls $account->getConsumer()->isPublished() and throws an OAuthUnauthorizedHttpException ("The client is disabled.") when it returns FALSE, so previously granted bearer tokens stop working as soon as their consumer is disabled. Kernel tests cover all three paths: rejecting an unpublished client at the client credentials grant, at the refresh token grant, and at resource access with an already-issued bearer token.

Upgrade

Update the drupal/consumers dependency to at least 1.24, which is where the consumer status field this feature relies on was introduced:

"drupal/consumers": "^1.24",

Any code relying on a disabled/unpublished consumer still being able to authenticate or use previously issued tokens will now be blocked; disable a consumer only when access should actually be revoked.
